newsitem.title: FRANCE: French government suspends airport extension work.
newsitem.headline: French government suspends airport extension work.

text.p: The French government on Thursday said it was suspending work on the 1.5 billion franc extension of Paris Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport and indicated that the choice of a third Paris area airport was still open.

In a statement, Transport Minister Jean-Claude Gayssot said that he had asked Senator Jean-Philippe Lachenaud to conduct a study this summer about the extension of Roissy airport and had decided to suspend work on the fourth runway which would have started on July 15.
"Air traffic is continuing to rise at five to six percent on average per year, while the actual capacity of the two large Paris airports is close to saturation," Gayssot said.

But he added that issues about noise and other disturbances by the traffic for people living near the airport were also very important as well as the regional distribution of the economic benefits of an airport.

He added a decision on a third Paris airport had not yet been taken. A spokeswoman for the minister said that even the site remained open while the previous government had expressed a preference for Beauvilliers, near Chartres, 80 km southwest of Paris.
A third airport would cost 50 to 100 billion francs.
